public_title: Your Joy Triggers Ancient Brain Networks
hook: You view play as a meaningless waste of time.

sections.title: Story
sections.narration: You view play as a meaningless waste of time. Ancient animals actually evolved playful games to build social trust millions of years ago. In 1998, neuroscientist Jaak Panksepp studied laboratory rats and recorded over 50,000 high pitched laughs per minute during rough play. The result? Joy is an ancient survival tool built deep inside the mammalian brain. Other studies on wild chimps and dolphins show the exact same social bonding pattern. Scientists call this universal drive the primary play system. So why do we assume play is just for young kids? Research shows adult brains need social games to reduce stress hormones rapidly. Does your brain stop needing joy when you grow up? No, the underlying neural pathways remain active for life. That's it. So next time you play a game, remember you view play as a meaningless waste of time.

claims.claim: Rats emit high-frequency ultrasonic vocalizations (laughter) during rough-and-tumble play, signaling positive affect.
Social play behavior activates subcortical neural circuits shared across mammalian species to facilitate social bonding.
